key_insight: Induction thermography detected micrometre-scale cracks in WC-10Co-4Cr coatings without destructive testing.
engineering_relevance: Non-invasive crack inspection could improve reliability and product quality in precision calender rollers, where coating damage threatens micrometre-level concentricity.
method: Test ground and as-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on C60 steel.
Induce cracks using mechanical strains of 0.12–0.4% and thermal shock.
Process induction thermography signals using Fourier transforms and principal component analysis.
evidence_signal: Minimum resolved crack widths were approximately 1 µm on ground surfaces and 1.7 µm on as-sprayed surfaces; deeper cracks produced stronger thermal contrast.
watch_item: Detection sensitivity depends on surface condition and crack geometry; these specimen results do not establish performance on full-scale rollers.
paper_title: Evaluation of Induction Thermography for the Detection of Cracks Due to Mechanical and Thermal Stress in WC-10Co-4Cr Coatings
